Additionally, `common/src/util/stats.ts` provides dependency-free statistical helpers including Wilson intervals, Newcombe's difference test, and chi-square sample-ratio-mismatch checks for experiment readouts. ai.title: Freestyle VM sandbox and terminal upstream guard for BuffBench
ai.summary: A new `--freestyle` flag lets BuffBench run each agent task in its own isolated Freestyle VM, which polls for completion and powers off automatically to prevent local sleep from tainting results. This mechanism ships the bench code and necessary environment variables to the VM while excluding eval answer files. Additionally, the `run_terminal_command` tool override now blocks commands that clone or fetch the evaluated repository's upstream, preventing agents from copying ground truth via the terminal. The repo setup also changed from a shallow clone with remotes to a detached fetch that leaves no remote pointing to the answer.

changes.what: Adds a Freestyle VM sandbox implementation that runs agent tasks in isolated virtual machines with automatic power-off and polling.
Wires the --freestyle flag into all main-*.ts entry points to select the VM sandbox over the local one.
Extends tool overrides to block terminal commands that access the upstream repository or its published packages.
Modifies cloneAtCommit to use a detached git fetch instead of a shallow clone with remotes, preventing remote-based answer retrieval.

eli5.text: The internal test suite that scores how well the coding assistant performs can now run each test in a separate, isolated virtual computer so that a sleeping laptop does not skew the timing results. It also blocks the assistant from downloading the answer key from the original source code repository, whether through a web link or by running a command in the terminal. This is a change to the internal testing tools only, so you will not notice any difference in how the application behaves for you.
